result.summary: This PR removes the M_ERROR mode from BlockValidationState and instead threads fatal/runtime errors through a new util::Expected<T, kernel::FatalError> return type across validation.cpp, node/blockstorage, the kernel C API, mining, RPC, and their call sites. It touches 41 files (+617/-384) across 5 commits and updates dozens of tests and benchmarks to match the new signatures. The stated goal is to stop conflating consensus-invalidity results with disk/system runtime errors in the same object, and to lay groundwork for a related refactor (#35570).
result.problem: BlockValidationState currently mixes two unrelated failure modes: consensus/policy invalidity (its actual purpose) and runtime errors (disk write failures, system errors) via M_ERROR. This forces every caller of ConnectBlock, AcceptBlock, ProcessNewBlock, and other functions to unwrap three possible outcomes from one object, and forces functions that never validate anything (FlushStateToDisk, DisconnectTip, ActivateBestChain) to take a BlockValidationState purely to report runtime errors.

result.card: This PR (RFC, Brainstorming label) reworks BlockValidationState to remove its M_ERROR mode, routing fatal/runtime errors instead through a new util::Expected<T, kernel::FatalError> type across validation.cpp, node/blockstorage, the kernel C API, mining, and RPC (+617/-384 across 41 files). The stated problem is that BlockValidationState conflates consensus-invalidity with disk/system errors, forcing every caller to unwrap three outcomes from one object; the author also frames it as groundwork for a related PR, #35570. The strongest evidence of importance is contested: reviewer optout21 gives only a qualified Concept ACK, flagging specific likely behavior changes (BlockChecked skipped on fatal error, dropped NONFATAL_UNREACHABLE checks) that remain unresolved, while maintainer maflcko questioned whether splitting errors out and then flattening them back to strings at RPC boundaries is worthwhile at all. CI is currently failing on the latest push, and the itemized review concerns from 2026-09-08 have no visible author reply as of the most recent force-push on 2026-09-17. No hard dependency blocks this PR, but it conflicts with numerous other open validation/mempool/mining PRs touching the same files, and it is explicitly positioned as enabling groundwork for #35570.
